narrative:
Your loan application was carefully reviewed, and the assessment found a 53% likelihood that you represent a credit risk — a figure that, while not dramatically high, was sufficient to result in a denial. This decision was not made lightly, and understanding the specific factors behind it may help you take meaningful steps toward a successful application in the future.

The single most influential factor working against your application was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, roughly half had no checking account at all, and only about one in five had a negative balance like yours. A negative checking account balance is a strong signal to the assessment system that your day-to-day finances may be under strain, and this concern weighed more heavily on the decision than any other factor.

The second most significant concern was the size of the loan you requested — 5,371 Deutsche Marks — which is nearly double the average amount requested by applicants who were approved, at around 2,887 DM. Given that average yearly salaries in Germany at the time ranged from 10,000 to 20,000 DM, this is a substantial sum, and the combination of a large loan amount with an already strained checking account raised the overall risk profile of your application considerably.

On a more positive note, the purpose of your loan — purchasing furniture and equipment — actually worked in your favor, nudging the assessment slightly toward a more favorable outcome. This is a common and generally well-regarded reason for borrowing, and it partially offset some of the concerns raised by the other factors.

It is also worth noting that your requested repayment period of 36 months is significantly longer than the average of about 19 months seen among approved applicants, and you already have two existing credits at this bank compared to an average of roughly 1.4 among those who were approved. While these factors were not among the top three drivers of this decision, they contribute to a broader picture of financial pressure.

To improve your chances in a future application, the most impactful step you could take would be to bring your checking account into a positive balance and maintain it there over time, as this was the strongest signal influencing the denial. You might also consider requesting a smaller loan amount, or exploring whether a shorter repayment term could make the application more favorable. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative about how to strengthen your financial profile before reapplying would be a worthwhile investment of your time.
